$comment: Teaching points the coverage map does not hold, because the worksheet types under them were made after it. Same fields as a coverage-map point (tp, grade, skill, code, strand). Kept few: a new type normally joins an existing point. A point marked `led` is taught by the teacher without a page (a routine with real objects, a number talk): it has no worksheet type by design.

points.skill: Plan and write a short story or message: a story map, a comic strip, a character description, a postcard
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100
Decode and encode a message with a key (picture code, number code, complete the key, make your own)
Say what can be measured about an object: how long, how heavy, how much it holds
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters with body benchmarks, then measure
Explain why a way of adding or subtracting works, with place value and blocks or a drawing
Read a first book made only of words the class can sound out and of taught heart words, and draw what each page says
Read a first picture book with purpose and understanding: sight words, a repeating sentence, and a picture for the new word
Say whether an outcome of drawing from a bag is certain, possible or impossible, and test a guess in an experiment with a tally and bars
Compare the chance of an outcome in two bags (more likely, less likely, the same) without fractions
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations, write the problem as one equation with a letter for the unknown, and check the answer against an estimate from rounded numbers
Ask and answer questions about key details in a short informational text and find the sentence that tells the answer
Name the main topic of an informational text and retell two or three key details that tell about it
Use headings, bold words, a caption and a glossary to find facts and word meanings in an informational text
Listen to a short fact text, read along, and answer questions about its key details with a picture
Name what a whole fact text is about and tell two key details of it
Tell which picture goes with which sentence of a fact text, and what the picture shows of it
Tell what comes first and what comes next in a fact text that tells a change
Name the main topic of an informational text of several paragraphs and what each paragraph is mostly about
Use headings, bold print, captions, a glossary, and an index to find facts in an informational text
Read a diagram with labels and arrows together with a text and tell what the diagram adds to the text
Describe the steps of a how-it-is-made text in order and tell why one step comes before another
Tell what two short fact texts on one topic both say and what only one of them says
Ask and answer questions about an informational text and show the paragraph and the sentence that prove each answer
Determine the main idea of an informational text of four paragraphs, recount the key details that support it, and tell what each paragraph is mostly about
Use the table of contents, headings, key words in bold, a sidebar, the glossary, and the index of a text to find information quickly
Describe how the events, steps, and ideas of an informational text connect, with words of time and sequence and of cause and effect
Ask and answer questions about a story and show the paragraph and the sentence that prove each answer
Retell a fable or folktale in order, determine its central message, and explain how the events of the story show it
Describe the characters of a story by their traits and feelings and explain how what they do leads to what happens next
Come to a group talk about a story prepared, and use notes and the story itself to explain ideas
Describe how a character in a story responds to a problem: what the character does and feels, and what happens because of it
Retell a fable by its beginning, middle, and end and tell the lesson it teaches
Ask and answer questions about key details in a short story and find the sentence that tells the answer
Describe the characters, the setting, and the big event of a story with key details
Retell a story by its beginning, middle, and end and tell the lesson it teaches
Find words in a story that tell how a character feels and words that appeal to the senses
Identify who is telling the story at different points: the narrator or one of the characters
Tell who a story is about, where it happens, and one big thing that happens in it
Retell a story heard aloud in order: the beginning, the middle, and the end
Answer who, where, what, and how questions about a story heard aloud, and ask a question about it
Match each part of a story heard aloud to the picture that shows it
Read and spell one-syllable words with a silent e, and tell how the e changes the vowel sound
Read and spell one-syllable words in which ai or ay spells long a
Read and spell one-syllable words in which ee or ea spells long e
Read and spell one-syllable words in which oa or ow spells long o
Read and spell one-syllable words with the digraphs ck and ng at the end and wh at the start
Read and spell one-syllable words that start with a consonant blend (s-blends, l-blends, r-blends)
Read and spell short-vowel words that end in a consonant blend (nd, mp, st, nk)
